subject: English
passage: The corporate restructuring proposal was released in 2019, outlining the company's response to financial pressures that had mounted since 2017. Written in formal business terminology that was unfamiliar to most factory workers but which was standard in communications with investors and regulatory agencies, the proposal notes that the company will not eliminate any manufacturing divisions, promises to maintain current safety standards—widely understood as a reassurance to union representatives—and positions the company as a model for other firms facing similar challenges (an implicit reference to the many competitors then struggling in the industry). So even though the proposal is explicitly addressed to company employees, it's reasonable to conclude that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: aspects of the proposal were modeled on similar documents from other companies.
choices.B: the union representatives may have been surprised by the proposal.
choices.C: the proposal actually had several intended audiences.
choices.D: many company employees opposed the restructuring and the proposal.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The passage tells us that the proposal was written in terminology important to investor and regulatory communications but not familiar to most factory workers, states that the proposal included "a reassurance to union representatives," and made implicit references to competitors in the industry. Because of the messages within the proposal that were largely irrelevant to company employees, we can assume that the company employees were not the only audience for this document.
